references.text: When Moses came down from Mount Sinai, his face shone after speaking with God. This is a parallel to Jesus' transfiguration, where his face was also changed during prayer.
Matthew's parallel account of the transfiguration on the mountain, where Jesus' face shone like the sun and his clothes became white as light.
Mark's parallel account of the transfiguration, where Jesus' clothes became dazzling white, whiter than anyone on earth could bleach them.
Peter testifies that he was an eyewitness to Jesus' majesty and glory on the holy mountain, a direct reference to the transfiguration on the mountain.
John's vision of the glorified Christ in Revelation, where his face was like the sun and his clothes were white – parallel to the transfiguration in Luke 9:29.
In Daniel's vision, a figure is described with a face like lightning and clothes of white linen, which recalls Jesus' transfigured appearance.
Paul writes that believers are transformed from glory to glory by reflecting the Lord's glory, a theological echo of the transfiguration.
Paul writes that Christ will transform our lowly body and make it like his glorious body, which was revealed at the transfiguration.
